name: Clockcard
short: Staff clock in from the van; the office watches the week fill up.
long: Two views of one clock. On a phone the fitter picks the job, taps clock in and gets a running timer, a break button and a note for the office. On the desk it is a week grid of people against days with overtime shaded, every job's hours set against the estimate, and a week that can be approved and exported.
proves: You find out a job is running over while it is still running, not when the invoice goes out.
features: Clock in, switch job, take a break, clock out — the timer runs against the real clock
Owner's week grid: people against days, overtime shaded, click a cell to correct an entry
Hours booked against the estimate for every job, over and under said in plain words
Approve or send a week back per person, then copy the payroll CSV out of a textarea
House rules — standard day, overtime thresholds, unpaid break, rounding — recalculate everything above
Clocking in on the phone shows up in the owner's grid and the job bars immediately
story: Most small firms find out a job ran over when they add up the invoice. This puts the clock in the fitter's pocket and the running total on the owner's screen at the same moment.
